origin: It means drawing things flat, without depth. It spread widely through Microsoft's Metro design for Windows Phone in 2010 and Apple's iOS 7 in 2013.
whenToUse: Simple screens read quickly on small displays.
Icons and color can carry the information hierarchy.
It must look the same across many devices.
whenNotToUse: You'd flatten things until pressable and non-pressable can't be told apart.
Layered screens that must show hierarchy through depth.
You'd rely on color alone to tell states apart.
accessibility: Give buttons enough contrast that a colored plane alone looks pressable.
State changes show with both color and words (Play, Pause).
Switches announce their on state with role=switch.
